title: The Use of Prompt Engineering in ChatGPT to Improve the Ability to Write Ethnoliteracy-Based Fiction Stories in Elementary Schools: A Quasi-Experimental Study
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether prompt engineering with ChatGPT can improve fifth-grade elementary students’ ability to write ethnoliteracy-based fiction stories. The study is motivated by persistent weaknesses in elementary students’ narrative writing, especially in structuring stories, developing characters and settings, and integrating local cultural values into writing. The authors argue that conventional instruction is often too generic and insufficiently engaging, while an ethnoliteracy approach may better connect writing tasks to students’ cultural identities.

The intervention combined generative AI with culturally grounded writing instruction. In the experimental condition, students used ChatGPT with structured prompts designed to support fiction writing around folklore and local cultural values; the control group received conventional fiction-writing instruction without AI assistance. The study used a quasi-experimental nonequivalent control group design with pretests and posttests. Participants were 50 fifth-grade students at Cimahi Mandiri 3 Public Elementary School in Cimahi City, West Java, Indonesia.

Results showed improvement in both groups, but the experimental group generally performed better on key indicators such as story structure, plot cohesion, setting, and incorporation of local cultural context. However, the reported N-gain scores were low in both groups, suggesting that overall gains were modest and that creative literacy development still requires sustained support. The authors conclude that ChatGPT-assisted prompt engineering, when paired with ethnoliteracy, can be a useful pedagogical strategy for elementary writing instruction, though it should be implemented thoughtfully and as part of ongoing guided practice.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's generative AI chatbot based on GPT-family large language models, used for interactive text generation and task support.
identified_tools.use_case: Used in a quasi-experimental intervention with structured prompt engineering to support 5th-grade elementary students in writing ethnoliteracy-based fiction stories, compared against conventional instruction without AI.

findings.finding_summary: The experimental group improved more than the control group on several fiction-writing indicators after ChatGPT-assisted prompt engineering, especially story structure, plot cohesion, setting, and integration of local cultural values. However, the reported N-gain was low in both groups (experimental=0.069; control=0.062), and the paper also reports a non-significant one-tailed t-test result, so overall impact is mixed/unclear despite descriptive gains.
findings.measure: Ethnoliteracy-based fiction story writing test scores; indicator-based rubric scores; N-gain; t-test

quality_tier_rationale: This is a quasi-experimental nonequivalent control group study with pretest/posttest and a non-AI comparator, which provides moderate causal evidence. However, the design is nonrandomized and the reported results are internally mixed, with low N-gain and a non-significant t-test reported.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports some meaningful descriptive improvements on specific writing indicators, but the aggregate gain is low and overall statistical evidence is unclear/mixed. That places the impact in the modest/unclear range rather than clearly positive medium or large impact.
